_patient.input_block:
73M, EW EMER. admission from EMERGENCY ROOM.
OUTCOME: discharged alive to CHRONIC/LONG TERM ACUTE CARE
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Bacteremia; Solitary pulmonary nodule; Nonspecific abnormal results of function study of kidney
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure; Acute and subacute bacterial endocarditis; Coronary atherosclerosis of autologous vein bypass graft; Congestive heart failure, unspecified; Streptococcus infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, streptococcus, group D [Enterococcus]; Atrial fibrillation; Unspecified essential hypertension; Other and unspecified hyperlipidemia
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Long-term (current) use of anticoagulants; Heart valve replaced by transplant
PROCEDURES: Right heart cardiac catheterization; Coronary arteriography using two catheters; Diagnostic ultrasound of heart
MEDICATIONS: Potassium Chloride 40mEq PO; Influenza Virus Vaccine 0.5mL IM; 5% Dextrose 250mL IV; Heparin Sodium 25,000UNIT IV; Furosemide 120mg IV; Torsemide 40mg PO; 0.9% Sodium Chloride (Mini Bag Plus) 100mL IV; Ampicillin Sodium 2g IV; Iso-Osmotic Dextrose 50mL IV; CeftriaXONE 2gm IV; Atorvastatin 40mg PO/NG; Aspirin 81mg PO/NG; Heparin Flush (10 units/ml) 2mL IV; Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 3mL IV; Pneumococcal Vac Polyvalent 0.5mL IM; Vancomycin 1000mg IV; Warfarin 2mg PO/NG; Heparin 7300UNIT IV; Mupirocin Nasal Ointment 2% 1Appl NU; Clindamycin 600mg IV; Metoprolol Tartrate 100mg PO/NG; Dabigatran Etexilate 150mg PO; 0.9% Sodium Chloride 1000mL IV
MICROBIOLOGY: BLOOD CULTURE: ENTEROCOCCUS FAECALIS [PENICILLIN G=S, AMPICILLIN=S, VANCOMYCIN=S, DAPTOMYCIN=S]
SERVICES: CMED
WARDS: Medicine/Cardiology; Emergency Department
_patient.note:
[1] The patient is a 73-year-old male presenting from the Emergency Room with bacteremia, a solitary pulmonary nodule, and nonspecific abnormal results of a function study of the kidney.
[2] The patient's primary diagnosis is acute on chronic diastolic heart failure.
[3] The patient's active diagnoses include acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, acute and subacute bacterial endocarditis, coronary atherosclerosis of autologous vein bypass graft, congestive heart failure, unspecified, Streptococcus infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, streptococcus, group D [Enterococcus], atrial fibrillation, unspecified essential hypertension, and other and unspecified hyperlipidemia.
[4] The patient's past medical history includes long-term (current) use of anticoagulants and heart valve replaced by transplant.
[5] Procedures performed include right heart cardiac catheterization, coronary arteriography using two catheters, and diagnostic ultrasound of the heart.
[6] Medications administered include Potassium Chloride 40mEq PO, Influenza Virus Vaccine 0.5mL IM, 5% Dextrose 250mL IV, Heparin Sodium 25,000UNIT IV, Furosemide 120mg IV, Torsemide 40mg PO, 0.9% Sodium Chloride (Mini Bag Plus) 100mL IV, Ampicillin Sodium 2g IV, Iso-Osmotic Dextrose 50mL IV, CeftriaXONE 2gm IV, Atorvastatin 40mg PO/NG, Aspirin 81mg PO/NG, Heparin Flush (10 units/ml) 2mL IV, Sodium Chloride 0.9% Flush 3mL IV, Pneumococcal Vac Polyvalent 0.5mL IM, Vancomycin 1000mg IV, Warfarin 2mg PO/NG, Heparin 7300UNIT IV, Mupirocin Nasal Ointment 2% 1Appl NU, Clindamycin 600mg IV, Metoprolol Tartrate 100mg PO/NG, Dabigatran Etexilate 150mg PO, and 0.9% Sodium Chloride 1000mL IV.
[7] Blood culture grew Enterococcus faecalis, which is sensitive to Penicillin G, Ampicillin, Vancomycin, and Daptomycin.
[8] The patient was managed by the CMED service on the Medicine/Cardiology ward in the Emergency Department.
[9] The patient was discharged alive to chronic/long term acute care.
